happening-2021.gazette: France criminalized abortion in 1920, and the ban held until 1975 — Annie Ernaux's student year of 1963 fell squarely inside that window. Her memoir supplies the film's procedure: doctors who would not write anything down, an address passed by word of mouth, the work itself done in a private flat. The law reached the helper and the helped alike.

parallel-mothers-2021.gazette: Volunteer teams began opening Civil War-era pits in Spain around the turn of the century, working from village memory and a shovel line before any statute obliged the state to help. The Historical Memory Law followed in 2007; the exhumations remain a live civic procedure rather than a closed chapter. Almodóvar routes his plot through that procedure instead of around it.

spencer-2021.gazette: The film opens by calling itself a fable from a true tragedy, which is a disclaimer and a thesis at once. Its three invented days at Sandringham sit inside a marriage that had already become public property by 1991, worked over in tabloids and, within months, in a biography Diana quietly cooperated with. Accuracy was never the instrument here; pressure was.
spencer-2021.prism: A fable gets to be wrong on purpose, but the license only pays off because the audience already knows the real timeline well enough to feel the distortion. The accuracy comes from the viewer's memory; the film just spends it.

summer-of-soul-2021.gazette: The Harlem Cultural Festival ran across six weekends in Mount Morris Park in the summer of 1969, and it was filmed properly, on multiple cameras. No broadcaster bought the tapes, so the reels sat in storage for roughly fifty years. The film cuts that footage against people who were there, watching themselves on a monitor for the first time.

the-hand-of-god-2021.gazette: Maradona's handled goal against England came on 22 June 1986 at the Estadio Azteca, while he was under contract to Napoli and the city treated him as municipal property. Sorrentino has said he stayed behind for a match rather than join his parents at the family house where they died of a gas leak. The film holds both events and the ordinary distance between them.

the-man-who-sold-his-skin-2021.gazette: Wim Delvoye tattooed a Swiss man's back over the better part of a year, then sold the finished work to a collector, with the man contracted to sit on exhibition at intervals and to have the skin removed and framed after his death. The film's opening card names that arrangement as its source. The living support is a term of the contract, not a metaphor.
the-man-who-sold-his-skin-2021.prism: The asset only appreciates while its carrier keeps walking around, which makes the collector's patience a strange sort of employment. Putting a refugee in that seat doesn't soften the ownership question — it just removes the option of walking away.

the-medium-2021.gazette: Shot as a documentary crew's field record, the film follows a hereditary shaman in Thailand's Isan region, where spirit-medium practice and inherited possession are ordinary parts of village religion rather than exotica. The consent conversations, the interview setups, the camera that arrives late to the important thing — all of it borrows the grammar of ethnographic film. Everything staged is staged inside a form that promises it was not.

the-souvenir-part-ii-2021.gazette: Joanna Hogg went through film school in Britain in the 1980s and made a graduation film there; Part II sends its heroine back through the same process, at the same kind of school, arguing with the same crew. Hogg cast Tilda Swinton as the mother of a character based on herself, and Swinton's daughter as the character. The restaging goes all the way down to the footage.

west-side-story-2021.gazette: San Juan Hill was a Black and Puerto Rican neighborhood on Manhattan's West Side until slum-clearance orders emptied it for Lincoln Center; the 1961 film shot in the half-demolished blocks left behind. Spielberg's version puts the wrecking ball in the first frame and keeps the eviction notices legible. The turf war is staged on land already scheduled to stop existing.
west-side-story-2021.prism: Whoever wins the rumble loses the block, which turns the fight from a plot engine into an obituary. The complex that replaced those streets is where the show gets revived.

all-quiet-on-the-western-front-2022.gazette: Matthias Erzberger signed the armistice in a railway carriage in the Forest of Compiègne on 11 November 1918, with the guns set to stop at eleven. The suicidal assault ordered into those last minutes is the film's own invention, present neither in Remarque nor in the record. Erzberger was shot dead by nationalists in 1921, for the signature.

all-the-beauty-and-the-bloodshed-2022.gazette: Nan Goldin's group P.A.I.N. staged die-ins on museum floors under the Sackler name, and the film runs that campaign against deposition video of the family answering for OxyContin. Goldin's own archive supplies the other half — the slideshow, the family photographs, her sister's institutional paperwork. The Met took the name off its galleries in 2021.

armageddon-time-2022.gazette: James Gray set his childhood film in Queens in 1980, at the private school he actually attended: Kew-Forest, whose board once included Fred Trump and whose pupils once included his son. The immigrant flight from Ukraine, the assimilating Jewish household, the grandfather's advice — all of it is drawn from Gray's own family. The Reagan campaign plays on the television behind a family that has just decided to protect its own.
armageddon-time-2022.prism: Memoir gives Gray the receipts to indict himself with: he was the boy who got the second chance while his friend got a record. The film treats that as evidence rather than as a defense.

broker-2022.gazette: Baby boxes exist in South Korea — a hatch in a church wall in Seoul where an infant can be left anonymously, with a bell that rings on the other side. Recorded use climbed after a 2012 adoption law required a birth to be registered before a child could be placed. Kore-eda builds a road movie out of that hatch and never once argues it away.

r-m-n-2022.gazette: In early 2020 a bakery in the Transylvanian village of Ditrău hired two workers from Sri Lanka, and the village organized against them: petitions, a public meeting, demands that the men be sent home. Mungiu keeps the sequence intact, including the part where people who had themselves gone abroad for work objected loudest. The film's long town-hall scene is that meeting, rebuilt.

suzume-2022.gazette: Suzume travels north through abandoned schools, a shuttered amusement park and towns that lost their populations; the doors in this film open only where people have already gone. The route ends on the Tohoku coast and in a child's diary whose entries stop in March 2011. The alert that sounds before each quake is the tone actually broadcast to phones across Japan.
suzume-2022.prism: Using the real alert means part of the audience flinches before the animation has done anything at all. That's the film's claim on the record: it isn't depicting the disaster so much as borrowing the reflexes it left behind.
